Tags work: any #word in a note becomes a tag, and the sidebar lists every tag with how many notes use it. All 17 automated tests pass, and every tag feature worked in the browser at desktop and phone sizes. I didn't find anything broken.

Filtering: click a tag to show only its notes, and click it again (or "Clear tag filter") to show all.
Suggestions: typing # in the editor suggests existing tags. Pick one with the arrow keys and Enter, or by clicking it. The suggestion box sits at the bottom of the editor, not next to where you're typing.
Renaming: the pencil on a tag renames it in the text of every note.
Display: tags appear as small chips in the preview.
What doesn't count as a tag:
headings like # Title
anything inside code
link addresses such as site.com/#section
number-only words like #2024
Capitals: tags ignore them, so #Work and #work are the same tag.
Renaming doesn't reorder notes: the edit times stay as they were, so the list keeps its order.

What I tested and how

Automated tests (7 new):
which words count as tags
counting notes per tag
renaming without touching #workout or code
spotting a tag being typed, then suggesting and inserting it
checking new tag names are valid
tags showing as chips without breaking apostrophes
Browser, both sizes: I made two notes tagged #work and #ideas, then checked:
Typing #wo suggested only "work", and Enter inserted it.
Typing #i and clicking "ideas" inserted it, and the cursor stayed in place so I could keep typing.
The sidebar showed "ideas 2" and "work 2".
Clicking "ideas" filtered the list to those two notes; clicking it again brought back all 3.
Renaming "work" to "job" changed it in both notes' text.
After a reload, the "job" tag was still there.
There were no page errors.
